hints: Focus on electrons lost and gained, since a redox equation must balance both atoms and charge.
Write the two half equations: $\text{Zn} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+} + 2e^-$ and $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Multiply the zinc half equation so both sides exchange the same 6 electrons, then check that Zn, Cr, H and charge all balance.
walkthrough:
**Write the two half-equations**

Think of this as two separate jobs. One species gives away electrons, the other collects them.

Oxidation (zinc loses electrons):
$$\text{Zn} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+} + 2e^-$$

Reduction (dichromate gains electrons in acid):
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Balance the electrons**

Electrons cannot appear in the overall equation, so what is lost must equal what is gained. Zinc gives 2, dichromate needs 6.

So we need 3 zinc atoms for every 1 dichromate ion:
$$3 \times (\text{Zn} \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+} + 2e^-)$$
Gives 6 electrons lost, matching the 6 electrons gained.

**Combine and check**

Add the scaled up zinc equation to the dichromate equation and cancel the electrons:
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 3\text{Zn} + 14\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{Zn}^{2+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Quick check: Cr 2 = 2, O 7 = 7, H 14 = 14, Zn 3 = 3. Charge left: $-2 + 14 = +12$. Charge right: $6 + 6 = +12$. Everything balances, so this is the correct equation.

options.A: Not balanced for electrons or charge. One $\text{Zn}$ only supplies $2e^-$ but the dichromate needs $6e^-$. Left charge is $+12$, right charge is $+8$, so electrons are missing.
options.B: Zinc atoms do not balance. There is 1 $\text{Zn}$ on the left but $3\text{Zn}^{2+}$ on the right. You cannot create extra zinc atoms, this tries to balance charge without balancing atoms.
options.C: Correct. Three $\text{Zn}$ atoms supply $6e^-$ which exactly matches the $6e^-$ needed to reduce one $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $2\text{Cr}^{3+}$. Atoms and charge both balance at $+12$ on each side.
options.D: Chromium and oxygen do not balance. Two $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ ions would give 4 Cr and 14 O, but the products show only 2 Cr and 7 O. The $14\text{H}^+$ and $7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ belong with one dichromate ion only.
